title: Isolation of Circular Single-Stranded DNA from Total DNA in Grapevine Samples
author: Vahid Jalali Javaran

steps.title: Prepare reaction mixture
steps.instruction: Combine the specified reagents for linear‑DNA removal in a microcentrifuge tube as indicated in the protocol.

steps.title: Remove linear DNA fragments
steps.instruction: Treat the mixture to degrade all linear DNA fragments (both double‑stranded and single‑stranded) generated during the restriction digestion, leaving predominantly circular single‑stranded DNA protected from exonuclease activity.

steps.title: Bead washing for purification
steps.instruction: Add magnetic beads at a 1.5 × ratio relative to the DNA solution volume, wash to remove residual contaminants, and recover the purified DNA.

steps.title: Synthesize complementary strand
steps.instruction: Set up a Klenow reaction to convert circular ssDNA into double‑stranded DNA, then purify the product.

substeps.instruction: Combine the circular ssDNA, appropriate buffer, Klenow DNA Polymerase I, and E. coli DNA Ligase in a clean microcentrifuge tube; mix gently to avoid DNA damage.
Incubate the reaction at 16 °C for 2.5 hours to allow strand synthesis and nick sealing.
Purify the synthesized dsDNA with magnetic beads (1.5 × bead ratio) and elute in 50 µL DNase‑free water.

steps.title: Linearize dsDNA with KpnI
steps.instruction: Digest the double‑stranded DNA to produce a linear fragment suitable for Nanopore library preparation, then clean the product.

substeps.instruction: Combine the dsDNA with KpnI restriction enzyme and the recommended buffer in a clean microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 hour to achieve complete digestion.
Perform a final magnetic‑bead wash (1.5 × bead ratio) to remove enzymes and buffers, then elute the purified linear DNA.

steps.title: Measure DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Use a Qubit fluorometer to determine DNA concentration; the reported yield in the protocol was approximately 4 µg.
